claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's my only child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. I also need to ask about your own circumstances.

Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Could you tell me which country you are currently living in, and what your circumstances are? For example:
- Are you working abroad temporarily?
- Are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces) posted overseas?
- Or have you moved abroad permanently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I've moved abroad - I'm not working for the Crown or anything like that, just living overseas now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the eligibility rules for Child Benefit, living in the UK is generally a key requirement to qualify.

The guidance mentions that you may be able to get Child Benefit if you "go to live in certain countries." To give you a complete assessment, could you tell me which country you have moved to? This will help me determine if there are any special arrangements that might apply to your situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know you're living in Spain. I have one more question that may be relevant to your situation.

Do you have either settled status or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme? Or are you perhaps receiving any UK benefits or National Insurance contributions while living in Spain?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any settled status or pre-settled status, and I'm not receiving any UK benefits or making National Insurance contributions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To summarise your situation:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 7 years old and lives with you
- You have moved abroad permanently to Spain
- You are not a Crown servant
- You do not have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You are not receiving UK benefits or making National Insurance contributions

Based on the eligibility rules, one of the key requirements for Child Benefit is that you **live in the UK**. While there are some exceptions for people who move abroad (such as Crown servants or those with certain connections to the UK through work, benefits, or the EU Settlement Scheme), none of these exceptions appear to apply to your circumstances.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to:
1. Be responsible for a child under 16 (or under 20 if in approved education/training)
2. Live in the UK

While Alex is 7 years old and lives with you (which meets the first requirement), you do not currently live in the UK. Although there are some exceptions that allow people living abroad to claim Child Benefit, none of these apply to your situation:

- You are not a Crown servant posted overseas
- You do not have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You are not receiving UK benefits or making National Insurance contributions while abroad

If your circumstances change in the future — for example, if you return to live in the UK — you would then be able to apply for Child Benefit for Alex.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. If you have any questions or if your circumstances change, please don't hesitate to reach out.
